title: AI UGC Video Ads Guide: What Makes One Work | AIVideosUGC
description: AI UGC video ads guide: plan a creator-style clip from one product photo, then add captions after download. Do not present the person as a real customer.
h1: AI UGC Video Ads Guide: Creator-Style Clips for Your Shop
lead: Make a creator-style clip from one product photo, and do not present the generated person as a real customer.
secondary_keywords: short video ads for small brands
summary: A creator-style ad is a short handheld scene of your product, made from one photo, with captions and music added by you.

paras: What a creator-style ad is, how to make one from a product photo, what the first frame should show, how long to make it, how to add your own captions, and why the person is not a customer.
sections.alt: Hands choose between two views of plain gray skincare jar on a bathroom shelf.

paras: Here, creator-style means the camera and the room: a handheld frame, ordinary daylight, and the product in someone's hands. The person is generated, so the clip is not a customer's review.

Sellers use this look on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts because it sits beside the posts people are already scrolling. Show the product in a kitchen, a bathroom, a desk, or a car. Keep your real product photos as well. This clip does not replace them.
sections.alt: Hands hold plain gray skincare jar beside a bathroom mirror and open its lid.

sections.h2: How to make UGC ads from a product photo in 3 steps
paras: Upload one clear photo, write one sentence for the scene, and download a clip you caption yourself.

A usable line for a gray jar: "An adult at a bright bathroom counter opens the jar, scoops a little onto the back of a hand, and turns the jar toward the phone." Leave on-screen words, famous faces, and logos you do not own out of the request. Those may be declined. The [Content Policy](/content) says what can be uploaded. Add captions yourself, because lettering drawn into the clip is often wrong.

[AI spokesperson video](page:spokesperson-videos) is the job when the clip is a person talking about one feature. [AI image to video](page:image-to-video) fits when you want motion from the still without a spoken part.
sections.alt: Hands scoop a small amount from plain gray skincare jar onto a hand.

sections.h2: What should a creator-style product video open on?
paras: The first frame should already show the product doing something. Do not open on an empty room or on a person with empty hands.
For a jar, open the lid, scoop a little product onto a hand, or hold the jar up to a mirror. One action per clip. A 10-second video has room for that moment and a little context, not a whole story.
sections.alt: Hands pull plain gray skincare jar from a tote onto a bathroom counter.

sections.h2: How long should AI video ads for TikTok be?
paras: Use 6 or 10 seconds for one action, 15 when the product has to be used, and 30 for a fuller demo. Pick 9:16 so the clip fills the phone.

Six seconds is a lid coming off. Ten seconds fits that action plus a second look. Fifteen can take the product out, use it, and set it down. Thirty leaves room for a longer demo. Those lengths cost 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits, shown before you start.

Use 1:1 for a square feed, 16:9 for a wide screen, and 3:4 or 4:3 when the placement asks for them. Each length or frame is a new clip. For a demo that shows the product in use, rather than one quick action, start with the [AI product video generator](page:product-videos).
sections.alt: Hands close plain gray skincare jar on a neutral bedroom dresser.

sections.h2: How do I finish short video ads for small brands?
paras: Treat the download as raw footage. Add captions, music, the price, and any code yourself. Captions are not added for you.

Put the words on in CapCut, TikTok, Canva, or Ads Manager so every character is yours. Keep the line short and away from the bottom and right edge of a vertical video, where the buttons sit. The upper middle of the frame is a safer spot. Use music you are allowed to run in an ad.
sections.alt: Hands hold plain gray skincare jar over a vanity beside a blank phone.

sections.h2: Can I present the person as someone who bought the product?
paras: No. Do not give them a name, a backstory, or a quote that says they purchased and reviewed it.
Keep the caption on what the product is and how it is used. Make another version when you want a different room or a different first action.
One photo, one action in the first frame, a length of 6 to 30 seconds, and your own captions and music you are allowed to use.
The person is generated. Say what the product does, not that a customer said so. A finished clip is commercially usable and has no watermark.

faq.q: Can I say the person in the video is a real customer?
faq.a: No. The person is generated, so do not give them a name or a quote that claims they bought the product. Write the caption about the product and how it is used.

faq.q: How long should a creator-style ad be?
faq.a: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Start with 6 or 10 for a single moment. Use 15 when the product is used on screen, and 30 for a longer demo.

faq.q: Which shape should a TikTok version use?
faq.a: Use 9:16. Use 1:1 for a square feed and 16:9 for a wide screen. 3:4 and 4:3 are available when the placement needs them.
No. Add captions, the price, and music after download so the spelling and the music license stay yours.

faq.q: How many credits does a 10-second clip use?
faq.a: A 10-second clip uses 40 credits. Six seconds is 24, fifteen is 60, and thirty is 120. A failed job returns the credits.

faq.q: What if the clip shows a part my product does not have?
faq.a: Do not post it. Make the clip again and name the exact action and the exact product in the sentence.

faq.q: Can I use the clip in a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. A finished clip is commercially usable and has no watermark. Add captions and music after download, and do not present the person as a customer.
